key_findings_en: Human Adenovirus C was detected in 9.4% (15/160) of all samples. Groundwater sources showed a detection frequency of 9.8% (12/122), with positive results in shallow tubular wells (12.9%), spring water (11.8%), deep tubular wells (11.1%), cisterns with rainwater (15.8%) and shallow dug wells (6.4%). [10.20935/acadimmunodis8447]

Human fecal contamination was the dominant source, as indicated by the consistent detection of HF183, which significantly increased during moderate and extreme rainfall events, indicating inputs from runoff and sewer overflows. [10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.130866]

Among 2,788 patients, the overall pathogen positivity rate was 64.56%. Twenty pathogens were identified, with human adenovirus (ADV) being the most prevalent. Mixed infections accounted for 48.28% of positive samples, with human adenovirus (ADV) and other pathogens as the most common combination. [10.1186/s12879-026-14054-3]

The patient achieved full clinical resolution without sequelae following supportive management with intravenous proton pump inhibitors, ophthalmic steroids, and respiratory support. [10.32677/ijch.v13i8.8413]

Complete or partial (>84%) HAdV-F41 genomes were recovered from wastewater samples, with mean coverage depths ranging from 103 to 105. The consensus sequences showed more than 99% similarity to reference genomes in the NCBI database. [10.1128/spectrum.00471-26]

papers.title: Human adenovirus detection in rural community water sources in central-west Brazil
papers.abstract: Introduction: Poor and limited access to improved water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, common in rural communities in developing countries, may lead to a high burden of enteric infections and the spread of fecal organisms. In the absence of a public water distribution network, rural areas obtain their water supply from surface and/or groundwater sources, where microbial quality is often unknown. Because adenoviruses are highly persistent in water and widely distributed in the environment, they have become an important group of enteric viruses and may potentially be involved in waterborne outbreaks. Materials and methods: A total of 160 water samples obtained from surface and groundwater sources in rural and traditional communities across Goiás, Brazil, were analyzed for the presence of Human Adenovirus C following viral concentration, nucleic acid extraction, and molecular detection. Results: Human Adenovirus C was detected in 9.4% (15/160) of the samples. Positive samples from groundwater sources had a frequency of 9.8% (12/122). Human adenovirus samples were also detected in samples from cisterns with rainwater (15.8%), deep tubular wells (11.1%), shallow tubular wells (12.9%), shallow dug wells (6.4%) and spring water (11.8%). No virus was found using the techniques adopted in the surface water and water truck samples. Conclusions: The results of this study highlight the need for greater investments in basic sanitation services in rural areas, in addition to supporting decision-makers in identifying water sources used by the population that may be contaminated. The identification and characterization of these pathogens are important for reducing public health risks associated with waterborne pathogens, especially in the State of Goiás.

In the absence of a public water distribution network, rural areas obtain their water supply from surface and/or groundwater sources, where microbial quality is often unknown. Because adenoviruses are highly persistent in water and widely distributed in the environment, they have become an important group of enteric viruses and may potentially be involved in waterborne outbreaks. Materials and methods: A total of 160 water samples obtained from surface and groundwater sources in rural and traditional communities across Goiás, Brazil, were analyzed for the presence of Human Adenovirus C following viral concentration, nucleic acid extraction, and molecular detection. Results: Human Adenovirus C was detected in 9.4% (15/160) of the samples. Positive samples from groundwater sources had a frequency of 9.8% (12/122). Human adenovirus samples were also detected in samples from cisterns with rainwater (15.8%), deep tubular wells (11.1%), shallow tubular wells (12.9%), shallow dug wells (6.4%) and spring water (11.8%). No virus was found using the techniques adopted in the surface water and water truck samples. Conclusions: The results of this study highlight the need for greater investments in basic sanitation services in rural areas, in addition to supporting decision-makers in identifying water sources used by the population that may be contaminated. The identification and characterization of these pathogens are important for reducing public health risks associated with waterborne pathogens, especially in the State of Goiás.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Poor access to water, sanitation and hygiene services in rural areas of developing countries may increase enteric infection burden and fecal pathogen spread. This study aimed to detect Human Adenovirus C in water sources used by rural communities in central-west Brazil to assess potential waterborne exposure risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 160 water samples were collected from surface and groundwater sources across rural and traditional communities in Goiás, Brazil, and analyzed for Human Adenovirus C. Samples were obtained from cisterns with rainwater, deep tubular wells, shallow tubular wells, shallow dug wells, spring water, surface water and water trucks.
analysis.methods: Viral concentration, nucleic acid extraction and molecular detection methods were applied to all water samples following standard laboratory protocols for the identification of Human Adenovirus C.
analysis.main_results: Human Adenovirus C was detected in 9.4% (15/160) of all samples. Groundwater sources showed a detection frequency of 9.8% (12/122), with positive results in shallow tubular wells (12.9%), spring water (11.8%), deep tubular wells (11.1%), cisterns with rainwater (15.8%) and shallow dug wells (6.4%). No virus was detected in surface water or water truck samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The detection of Human Adenovirus C across multiple groundwater source types indicates widespread low-level contamination of drinking water supplies in these rural communities. This study provides baseline surveillance data on adenoviral contamination of private water sources in Goiás where public water distribution networks are absent.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the need for pathogen surveillance in rural water sources and inform water safety interventions in underserved communities. Targeted monitoring of groundwater sources may help reduce public health risks associated with waterborne adenoviral exposure in the region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This cross-sectional survey provides prevalence data but cannot establish temporal patterns of contamination or source attribution. The study focused solely on Human Adenovirus C and molecular detection methods may have limited sensitivity compared to cell culture isolation. Evidence strength is moderate given the descriptive nature and absence of epidemiological linkage to clinical cases.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study analyzed 160 water samples from rural communities in Goiás, Brazil to detect Human Adenovirus C. Using viral concentration, nucleic acid extraction and molecular detection, the study found Human Adenovirus C in 9.4% of samples overall, with groundwater sources showing 9.8% detection. Positive samples came from cisterns with rainwater (15.8%), shallow tubular wells (12.9%), spring water (11.8%), deep tubular wells (11.1%) and shallow dug wells (6.4%), while surface water and water trucks tested negative. The findings indicate low-level but widespread adenoviral contamination of private groundwater sources used for drinking water supply. The authors emphasize the need for improved basic sanitation services and pathogen surveillance to reduce waterborne exposure risks in these underserved rural populations without access to public water distribution networks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 发展中国家农村地区获得水、环境卫生和个人卫生服务的机会不佳可能会增加肠道感染负担和粪便病原体传播。本研究旨在检测巴西中西部农村社区使用的水源中的 人腺病毒 C,以评估潜在的水传播风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 从巴西戈亚斯州农村和传统社区的地表水和地下水源采集了总共 160 个水样,并进行了 人腺病毒 C 分析。样品取自雨水蓄水池、深管井、浅管井、浅挖井、泉水、地表水和运水车。
elements_zh.methods: 按照标准实验室方案对所有水样进行病毒浓缩、核酸提取和分子检测方法,以鉴定 人腺病毒 C.
elements_zh.main_results: 所有样品中 9.4% (15/160) 检测到 人腺病毒 C。地下水源检测频率为9.8%(12/122),其中浅管井(12.9%)、泉水(11.8%)、深管井(11.1%)、雨水蓄水池(15.8%)和浅挖井(6.4%)呈阳性。地表水或运水车样本中未检测到病毒。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在多种地下水源类型中检测到 人腺病毒 C 表明这些农村社区的饮用水供应存在广泛的低水平污染。本研究提供了缺乏公共配水网络的戈亚斯州私人水源腺病毒污染的基线 监测 数据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了农村水源中对病原体 监测 的需求,并为服务欠缺社区的水安全干预措施提供了信息。对地下水源进行有针对性的监测可能有助于降低该地区与水传播腺病毒暴露相关的公共卫生风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这项横断面调查提供了 患病率 数据,但无法确定污染的时间模式或来源归因。该研究仅关注 人腺病毒 C,与细胞培养分离相比,分子检测方法的灵敏度可能有限。鉴于其描述性且缺乏与临床病例的流行病学联系,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:在发展中国家的农村社区,获得改善的水、环境卫生和个人卫生 (WASH) 服务的机会很差且有限,这可能会导致肠道感染和粪便生物传播的沉重负担。在缺乏公共供水网络的情况下,农村地区从地表水和/或地下水源获取供水,而这些水源的微生物质量往往未知。由于腺病毒在水中具有高度持久性,并且在环境中广泛分布,因此它们已成为肠道病毒的重要类群,并可能潜在地参与水传播的暴发。材料和方法:通过病毒浓缩、核酸提取和分子检测,对从巴西戈亚斯州农村和传统社区的地表水和地下水源获取的总共 160 个水样进行了 人腺病毒 C 的存在分析。结果:在 9.4% (15/160) 的样品中检测到 人腺病毒 C。地下水源的阳性样本频率为 9.8% (12/122)。雨水蓄水池(15.8%)、深管井(11.1%)、浅管井(12.9%)、浅挖井(6.4%)和泉水(11.8%)的样品中也检测到了人腺病毒样品。使用地表水和洒水车样本中采用的技术没有发现病毒。结论:本研究的结果强调,除了支持决策者确定可能受到污染的人口使用的水源外,还需要对农村地区的基本卫生服务进行更多投资。这些病原体的识别和表征对于减少与水传播病原体相关的公共卫生风险非常重要,特别是在戈亚斯州。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 发展中国家农村地区获得水、环境卫生和个人卫生服务的机会不佳可能会增加肠道感染负担和粪便病原体传播。本研究旨在检测巴西中西部农村社区使用的水源中的 人腺病毒 C,以评估潜在的水传播风险。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 从巴西戈亚斯州农村和传统社区的地表水和地下水源采集了总共 160 个水样,并进行了 人腺病毒 C 分析。样品取自雨水蓄水池、深管井、浅管井、浅挖井、泉水、地表水和运水车。
analysis_zh.methods: 按照标准实验室方案对所有水样进行病毒浓缩、核酸提取和分子检测方法,以鉴定 人腺病毒 C.
analysis_zh.main_results: 所有样品中 9.4% (15/160) 检测到 人腺病毒 C。地下水源检测频率为9.8%(12/122),其中浅管井(12.9%)、泉水(11.8%)、深管井(11.1%)、雨水蓄水池(15.8%)和浅挖井(6.4%)呈阳性。地表水或运水车样本中未检测到病毒。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在多种地下水源类型中检测到 人腺病毒 C 表明这些农村社区的饮用水供应存在广泛的低水平污染。本研究提供了缺乏公共配水网络的戈亚斯州私人水源腺病毒污染的基线 监测 数据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了农村水源中对病原体 监测 的需求,并为服务欠缺社区的水安全干预措施提供了信息。对地下水源进行有针对性的监测可能有助于降低该地区与水传播腺病毒暴露相关的公共卫生风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这项横断面调查提供了 患病率 数据,但无法确定污染的时间模式或来源归因。该研究仅关注 人腺病毒 C,与细胞培养分离相比,分子检测方法的灵敏度可能有限。鉴于其描述性且缺乏与临床病例的流行病学联系,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Sources and dynamics of fecal pollution and antibiotic resistance across a Mediterranean land-sea continuum.
papers.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of fecal pollution dynamics and associated antibiotic resistance is critical for effective water quality management in coastal watersheds exposed to strong hydrological variability. This study aimed to identify the relative contribution of human and animal fecal sources, assess the spatial and temporal distribution of contamination, and evaluate the occurrence of selected antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) across a Mediterranean land-sea continuum (central Adriatic Sea, Italy) under contrasting rainfall conditions. Surface water and sediment samples were collected during the bathing season and analyzed using host-associated microbial source tracking (MST) markers and selected ARGs. Human fecal contamination was the dominant source, as indicated by the consistent detection of HF183, which significantly increased during moderate and extreme rainfall events, indicating inputs from runoff and sewer overflows. The presence of human adenovirus (HAdV) further supported sewage-derived contamination, whereas animal-associated markers showed lower detection frequencies and more heterogeneous spatial patterns. ARGs, including tetracycline resistance genes tetM, were widely detected, with generally higher concentrations at freshwater sites. While ARG distribution was influenced by hydrological variability, tetM showed lower temporal variability and remained relatively abundant under drought conditions, suggesting longer-term environmental persistence. Rainfall emerged as a major driver shaping marker distribution, with water showing high temporal variability and sediments acting as secondary reservoirs enriched during heavy rainfall events. These findings provide relevant insights for improving water quality strategies and support targeted management actions to mitigate fecal pollution in Mediterranean coastal systems.

papers.source_body_en: A comprehensive understanding of fecal pollution dynamics and associated antibiotic resistance is critical for effective water quality management in coastal watersheds exposed to strong hydrological variability. This study aimed to identify the relative contribution of human and animal fecal sources, assess the spatial and temporal distribution of contamination, and evaluate the occurrence of selected antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) across a Mediterranean land-sea continuum (central Adriatic Sea, Italy) under contrasting rainfall conditions. Surface water and sediment samples were collected during the bathing season and analyzed using host-associated microbial source tracking (MST) markers and selected ARGs. Human fecal contamination was the dominant source, as indicated by the consistent detection of HF183, which significantly increased during moderate and extreme rainfall events, indicating inputs from runoff and sewer overflows. The presence of human adenovirus (HAdV) further supported sewage-derived contamination, whereas animal-associated markers showed lower detection frequencies and more heterogeneous spatial patterns. ARGs, including tetracycline resistance genes tetM, were widely detected, with generally higher concentrations at freshwater sites. While ARG distribution was influenced by hydrological variability, tetM showed lower temporal variability and remained relatively abundant under drought conditions, suggesting longer-term environmental persistence. Rainfall emerged as a major driver shaping marker distribution, with water showing high temporal variability and sediments acting as secondary reservoirs enriched during heavy rainfall events. These findings provide relevant insights for improving water quality strategies and support targeted management actions to mitigate fecal pollution in Mediterranean coastal systems.

papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing of adenovirus 41 directly from wastewater using nested overlapping PCR and MinION
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human adenovirus F41 (HAdV-F41) is one of the leading causes of children’s acute gastroenteritis and was recently linked to an outbreak of severe acute hepatitis of unknown etiology among children during 2021 to 2022. While most evidence is based on clinical data, wastewater-based epidemiology offers a community-level approach to monitoring circulating strains and enhancing outbreak preparedness. In this study, we developed an overlapping amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing approach to directly detect HAdV-F41 from archived wastewater samples, using nested PCR with 13 primer sets. Archived wastewater samples were collected between 2021 and 2022 from three treatment plants in Seattle, USA. The viral load ranged from 1.2 × 10 3 to 8.4 × 10 3 genome copies per liter. The Oxford Nanopore platform was used for whole-genome sequencing. Complete or partial (>84%) HAdV-F41 genomes were recovered from wastewater samples, with mean coverage depths ranging from 103 to 105. The consensus sequences showed more than 99% similarity to reference genomes in the NCBI database. The phylogenetic analysis revealed that 2 sequences clustered within lineage 2a and 11 within lineage 2b, reflecting that at least two sub-lineages were circulating in the community at that time. Our results demonstrate that the overlapping amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing approach using the Oxford Nanopore platform reliably recovers HAdV-F41 genomes from wastewater. This method offers high-resolution genomic surveillance of circulating, clinically relevant HAdV-F41, supporting wastewater-based epidemiology as a valuable tool for detecting emerging variants and strengthening the early warning system for future disease outbreaks. IMPORTANCE Human adenovirus F41 is a primary cause of childhood gastroenteritis and has been linked to recent outbreaks of severe acute hepatitis in children, yet community-level genomic surveillance of this virus remains limited. This study shows that wastewater can be used to recover nearly complete HAdV-F41 genomes through a targeted overlapping-amplicon sequencing strategy on the Oxford Nanopore platform. By applying this method to archived wastewater samples, we detected the simultaneous circulation of multiple viral lineages in a large city. These findings extend wastewater-based epidemiology beyond SARS-CoV-2 and emphasize its importance for monitoring clinically significant enteric viruses. The method described here offers a scalable tool for tracking viral evolution in communities and enhancing early warning systems for future outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人腺病毒 F41 (HAdV-F4​​1) 是儿童急性胃肠炎的主要原因之一,最近与 2021 年至 2022 年儿童中不明原因重症急性肝炎 暴发 有关。该研究旨在开发一种直接检测废水中 HAdV-F4​​1 的方法,以增强社区层面的 基因组监测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用基于重叠扩增子的全 基因组 测序方法,从 2021 年至 2022 年从美国西雅图的三个 治疗 工厂收集的存档废水样本中直接检测 HAdV-F4​​1。该方法应用于样品以回收几乎完整的 HAdV-F4​​1 基因组。
elements_zh.methods: 存档的废水样本是在 2021 年至 2022 年期间从美国西雅图的三个 治疗 工厂收集的。Oxford Nanopore 平台用于全 基因组 测序。采用具有 13 个引物组的巢式重叠 PCR 方法对病毒 基因组 进行扩增和测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 从废水样品中回收了完整或部分 (>84%) HAdV-F4​​1 基因组,平均覆盖深度范围为 103 至 105。共有序列与 NCBI 数据库中的参考 基因组 相似性超过 99%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 系统发育分析显示,有2个序列聚集在谱系2a内,11个序列聚集在谱系2b内,反映出当时至少有两个亚谱系在群落中流传。此方法提供了一种可扩展的工具,用于跟踪社区中的病毒 进化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这里描述的方法提供了一个可扩展的工具,用于跟踪社区中的病毒 进化 并增强未来 暴发 的预警系统。它支持基于废水的 流行病学 作为检测 HAdV-F4​​1 新兴变种的宝贵工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。证据强度很高,因为该方法是通过废水样品的直接测序进行验证的,并且与参考 基因组 具有高度相似性。

papers.title: Pharyngoconjunctival Fever with Atypical Gastrointestinal and CutaneousManifestations: A Pediatric Case Report
papers.abstract: Pharyngoconjunctival fever (PCF) is a distinct clinical syndrome characterized by high fever, pharyngitis, and non-purulent conjunctivitis, typically following human adenovirus (HAdV) infection. While adenovirus is generally a self-limiting condition in immunocompetent patients, it can present as a "Pandora’s box" of atypical systemic complications. This report describes a 10-year-old male presenting with the classic PCF triad alongside significant hematemesis and a widespread maculopapular rash. The clinical course was complicated by respiratory distress requiring supplemental oxygen and two episodes of gastrointestinal hemorrhage (~500 mL) followed by melena. Diagnostic confirmation was achieved via polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of throat and conjunctival swabs, which were positive for Adenovirus. Laboratory investigations ruled out common differentials including Dengue, Kawasaki disease, and Scarlet fever. Following supportive management with intravenous proton pump inhibitors, ophthalmic steroids, and respiratory support, the patient achieved full clinical resolution without sequelae. This case highlights the necessity for clinicians to recognize gastrointestinal and cutaneous manifestations as rare but possible components of the PCF spectrum to avoid diagnostic delays and ensure appropriate supportive intervention.

papers.title: Analysis of the pathogenic spectrum and epidemiological characteristics of 22 respiratory pathogens in Zhuhai City, China, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Effective surveillance of respiratory infectious diseases is crucial for precise prevention and evidence-based public health response. This study analyzed the etiological spectrum of respiratory pathogens in Zhuhai, a high-mobility port city, from January 2024 to December 2025. Methods Throat swab specimens from national sentinel influenza-like illness (ILI) cases and hospitalized severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases were tested for 22 pathogens using real-time PCR. Descriptive epidemiological methods were applied. Results Among 2,788 patients, the overall pathogen positivity rate was 64.56%. Twenty pathogens were identified, with Streptococcus pneumoniae (SP), Haemophilus influenzae (Hi), human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A virus (FluA), human adenovirus (ADV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) being the most prevalent. Mixed infections accounted for 48.28% of positive samples, with SP + Hi as the most common combination. Positivity rates for HRV, SP, and Hi were significantly higher in males, while MP was higher in females. Children aged 0–14 years constituted 96.11% of positive cases, with the highest rate in the 4–14 years group. Monthly trends showed SP and Hi were persistently dominant with synchronized peaks. FluA exhibited several epidemic peaks. HRV circulated sporadically, while MP and ADV peaked from May to September 2024. Conclusions In this study, multiple respiratory pathogens co-circulated in Zhuhai during 2024–2025, with distinct patterns by sex, age, and season. Children under 15 were the primary affected population, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance in this group.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 有效的呼吸道传染病监测对于精准预防和循证公共卫生应对至关重要。本研究分析了高流动性港口城市珠海市2024年1月至2025年12月的呼吸道病原体病原谱。方法采用实时PCR技术对全国哨点流感样病例(ILI)病例和住院严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)病例的咽拭子标本进行22种病原体检测。应用描述性流行病学方法。结果 2788例患者中,总体病原阳性率为64.56%。鉴定出 20 种病原体,其中肺炎链球菌 (SP)、流感嗜血杆菌 (Hi)、人鼻病毒 (HRV)、甲型流感病毒 (FluA)、人腺病毒 (ADV) 和肺炎支原体 (MP) 最为常见。混合感染占阳性样本的48.28%,其中SP+Hi是最常见的组合。男性的 HRV、SP 和 Hi 阳性率显着较高,而女性的 MP 阳性率较高。0-14岁儿童占阳性病例的96.11%,其中4-14岁儿童比例最高。月度趋势显示 SP 和 Hi 持续占据主导地位,峰值同步。甲型流感出现了几个流行高峰。HRV 呈零星传播,而 MP 和 ADV 在 2024 年 5 月至 9 月达到峰值。结论 在本研究中,2024 年至 2025 年期间,多种呼吸道病原体在珠海共同传播,且按性别、年龄和季节呈现不同的模式。15 岁以下儿童是主要受影响人群,这突出表明该群体需要有针对性的 监测。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 有效的呼吸道传染病监测对于精准预防和循证公共卫生应对至关重要。本研究旨在分析珠海这个高流动性港口城市2024-2025年呼吸道病原体的病原学谱。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了珠海这座高流动性港口城市2024年1月至2025年12月的呼吸道病原体病原谱。采用实时PCR技术对全国哨点流感样病例(ILI)病例和住院严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)病例的咽拭子标本进行了22种病原体检测。
analysis_zh.methods: 应用描述性流行病学方法来分析数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 2788例患者中,总体病原阳性率为64.56%。已鉴定出 20 种病原体,其中 人腺病毒 (ADV) 最为流行。混合感染占阳性样本的48.28%,其中人腺病毒(ADV)与其他病原体的组合为最常见的组合。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, September 5, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Five-year study reveals molecular features of adenovirus in hospitalized children by Bioengineer September 4, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Human adenovirus, one of the most important viral causes of childhood respiratory illness worldwide, has been mapped in unprecedented clinical detail in a new five-year study from northern China. Drawing on more than 42,000 hospitalized children with respiratory tract infections, researchers at Hebei Children’s Hospital and Hebei Medical University have shown that two specific genotypes of the virus dominate severe pediatric disease in the region, that viral co-infections are strikingly common, and that one genotype in particular, HAdV-7, leaves a distinctive and dangerous immunological fingerprint in young patients. The findings, published in Virology Journal, offer clinicians a molecular roadmap for identifying which children are most at risk of life-threatening adenovirus pneumonia. The retrospective study analyzed clinical data from 42,044 children admitted to Hebei Children’s Hospital between 2016 and 2020. Sputum samples collected at admission were tested for viral nucleic acids, and positive samples underwent genotyping to determine which adenovirus types were circulating. The researchers combined this molecular surveillance with demographic records, clinical symptoms, and a battery of laboratory indicators, including inflammatory markers, immune cell indices, and measures of cardiac and liver injury. Statistical comparisons relied on chi-squared tests for categorical differences and non-parametric tests, including the Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, for continuous variables, while phylogenetic relationships among viral sequences were reconstructed using the neighbor-joining method. The headline figure is sobering: 3,123 of the 42,044 samples—7.43 percent—tested positive for human adenovirus. But the more surprising number was what came with it. Of the adenovirus-positive children, 1,954, or 62.6 percent, carried at least one additional respiratory pathogen, a phenomenon the authors call viral co-detection. Human rhinovirus was the most frequent companion, followed by respiratory syncytial virus and human parainfluenza virus. This high rate of co-infection complicates the traditional picture of adenovirus as a standalone agent of pediatric pneumonia and suggests that in many hospitalized children, adenovirus is part of a polymicrobial assault on the respiratory tract rather than a solitary invader. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - September 3, 2026) - DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. (CSE: DTR) (FSE: X8F) ("DiagnosTear" or the "Company"), a developer of innovative point-of-care eye diagnostic solutions, is pleased to announce the submission of a pre-submission request to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") for its TeaRxTM Red Eye diagnostic test (the "Pre-Submission"). The Pre-Submission represents an important regulatory milestone in the Company's U.S. development strategy for TeaRxTM Red Eye. DiagnosTear is seeking FDA's input on the product's regulatory pathway and data development plan. TeaRxTM Red Eye is being developed as a rapid, point-of-care test to aid healthcare professionals in differentiating between adenoviral conjunctivitis, ocular herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection, and allergic conjunctivitis in symptomatic adult and paediatric patients presenting with red-eye symptoms. TeaRxTM Red Eye is being developed for use in point-of-care settings by general practitioners, ophthalmologists, optometrists, and trained healthcare personnel. Red eye is one of the most common reasons for visits to primary care and ophthalmology clinics, yet different causes can present with overlapping symptoms while requiring substantially different treatment and infection-control approaches. TeaRxTM Red Eye is designed to provide rapid results at the point of care to support differential diagnosis and help clinicians make more informed treatment decisions. The Pre-Submission was prepared and submitted with the support of Hogan Lovells Cadwalader US LLP, which is serving as DiagnosTear's U.S. regulatory counsel. The firm's team involved in the submission includes experienced legal and regulatory professionals supporting medical device and in-vitro diagnostic regulatory matters. "The submission of our first FDA Pre-Submission for TeaRxTM Red Eye is an important milestone toward bringing our technology to the U.S. market," said Dr. Shimon Gross, CEO of DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. "By engaging with FDA at this stage, we aim to establish a clear regulatory pathway and align our clinical and analytical development program with the Agency's expectations. We are pleased to be working with the experienced Hogan Lovells Cadwalader team as we advance this process." TeaRxTM Red Eye builds on DiagnosTear's strategy to develop rapid, multi-parametric tear-based diagnostics that can be used directly at the point of care. About DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. is focused on the development and commercialization of rapid, point-of-care, multi-parametric diagnostic tests for ocular diseases. By leveraging the analysis of tear fluid composition, DiagnosTear provides innovative solutions for diagnosing conditions including Dry Eye and Red Eye. The Company is committed to improving patient outcomes and transforming ophthalmic care through advanced, accessible diagnostic technologies. news.content: DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. Announces Private Placement of Units 4 min read DTR 0 Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - August 31, 2026) - DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. DTR (FSE: X8F) (" DiagnosTear " or the " Company ") is pleased to announce it will be proceeding with a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,800,000 units (" Units ") at a price of C$0.50 per Unit for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$1,400,000 (the " Offering "). The Company expects BioLight Life Sciences Ltd., parent company of DiagnosTear, and Elcam Medical Ltd. to each participate for up to one-third of the total Offering. Each Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a " Common Share ") and one common share purchase warrant (a " Warrant" ). Each Warrant will be exercisable to purchase one Common Share at an exercise price of C$1.00 for a term of twelve (12) months from the closing date of the Offering. No finder's fees will be paid in connection with this Offering. The net proceeds of the Offering will be used for the Company's working capital and general corporate purposes. All securities to be issued, subject to occurrence of the closing of the Offering, will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day after the issuance thereof. Closing of the Offering is subject to approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange. Certain insiders of the Company may acquire Units in the Offering. Any participation by insiders in the Offering would constitute a "related party transaction" as defined under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (" MI 61-101 "). However, the Company expects such participation would be exempt from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 as neither the fair market value of the Units subscribed for by the insiders, nor the consideration for the Units paid by such insiders, would exceed 25% of the Company's market capitalization. None of the securities sold in connection with the Offering will be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and no such securities may be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from the registration requirements. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy nor shall there be any sale of the securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. On Behalf of the Board of Directors: Yifftach Biel, Chief Financial Officer DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. For further information, please contact: Dr. Shimon Gross, Chief Executive Officer DiagnosTear Technologies Inc. Email: shimon@diagnostear.com Tel: +972-523408550 About DiagnosTear DiagnosTear is a leading ophthalmic company developing and commercializing disruptive diagnostic solutions for better management of eye diseases. DiagnosTear's TeaRxTM technology is a diagnostic platform intended for rapid, Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) of ophthalmic pathologies through multi-parameter analysis of non-invasively collected tear fluid. The first CE-IVD, and Israeli MoH-approved test based on the TeaRxTM platform is intended for diagnosis of Dry Eye Syndrome (DES TeaRxTM Dry Eye). This product is not FDA-cleared yet. Beyond DES, DiagnosTear is developing innovative tests based on the TeaRxTM platform for additional ophthalmic indications. Among others, DiagnosTear's pipeline includes TeaRxTM Red Eye: The first test of its kind for differential assessment of adenoviral conjunctivitis, Herpetic Keratitis and Allergic conjunctivitis. For additional information about DiagnosTear, please visit https://diagnostear.com . news.source_body_en: DiagnosTear Technologies Inc., based in Vancouver, British Columbia, announced on August 31, 2026, a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,800,000 units at C$0.50 per unit, aiming to raise up to C$1,400,000 for working capital and general corporate purposes. The units consist of common shares and purchase warrants, with the Company expecting participation from BioLight Life Sciences Ltd. and Elcam Medical Ltd., each potentially subscribing for up to one-third of the total offering. The Offering is subject to approval by the Canadian Securities Exchange, and the Company anticipates that insider participation may be exempt from certain requirements. The development of the TeaRxTM platform includes tests for ophthalmic conditions such as Dry Eye Syndrome and adenoviral conjunctivitis, though FDA clearance for some products is pending. The announcement highlights the Company's focus on diagnostic solutions for eye diseases, with the TeaRxTM technology designed for rapid, point-of-care testing of non-invasively collected tear fluid. The event is a financial update rather than a public health outbreak, as no confirmed or suspected cases of human adenovirus infection are reported in the evidence.
